Iconic ‘90s Burger Yacht Sold for Less Than the Cost of Its Midlife Restoration
24 photos
Photo: IYC
A yacht can have several lives, and that always depends on how well its owners treat it. This 1998 raised pilothouse yacht from one of the greatest American yacht builders of all time is still a collector’s item, even though its newest owner grabbed it at a bargain price.
Less than a year ago, Silver Seas was marketed at almost $6 million; this month, it sold for less than $5 million. Sadly, as enormous megayachts and new-generation superyachts with all kinds of innovation, including those related to cleaner propulsion, take center stage, the ‘80s and ‘90s yachts being to look outdated and simply not big enough for the needs (and ego) of contemporary millionaires.
However, a yacht like Silver Seas will always have its fair share of admiration , no matter what, simply because it’s a Burger, and this all-American brand has earned a loyal following. Silver Seas is particularly interesting for yachting connoisseurs in general, and Burger followers especially, for being the largest open flybridge Burger designed by the legendary Don O’Keeffe in operation.
At the time of its delivery, in the Fall of 1998, it was officially the largest Burger ever built. The 107-footer (32.7 meters) may seem small by today’s superyacht standards, but it was a considerable upgrade for its owners at the time, who eventually moved on to an even bigger yacht from the same builder.
Photo: IYC Those famous original owners were none other than Tom and Grace Benson, owners of the NFL New Orleans Saints football team. Having previously owned and enjoyed a smaller, 88-foot Burger named Lady Grace (in honor of Grace Benson), they felt ready to upgrade to a bigger, more comfortable version, which would be named Lady Grace Marie.
Tom Benson was one of those serial yacht owners who stay faithful to a particular brand, and he even compared Burger yachts to Mercedes Benz cars, in terms of how both brands are able to deliver a proven DNA and still make continuous upgrades.
The new 107-foot Burger had a spectacular life ahead, as the Benson’s pleasure craft. It would travel to the Bahamas and Caribbean, return to New Orleans for the football season, and then cruise to Rockport (the Benson’s vacation town), and to Maine, during the summer.
The NFL boss had specific requirements for his bigger yacht, such as ample side decks, a bigger aft deck, and the engine room moved aft. Style-wise, the owners (Mrs. Grace in particular) envisioned an interior that would reflect the extensive time they had spent in Asia. They worked closely with Douglas Richey, the in-house interior designer for Burger at the time, to create an interior with clear Far East influences, but still classic in a timeless way.
Photo: IYC Shoji panels, tumbled limestone tile, and etched glass were defining elements of the original Lady Grace Marie’s aesthetic, before Japanese-style superyacht interiors became trendy. The Japanese “Shu” symbol, translated as “Welcome”, was seen everywhere onboard Lady Grace Marie.
Aside from the beautiful Japanese-inspired interior design, Lady Grace Marie sported significant engineering upgrades that made it one of the top luxury yachts launched in 1998. Things like a hydraulic passerelle, an Atlas Shorepower conversion system, and stainless steel fuel piping with swagelock fittings throughout, were premium innovations for the industry at that time.
Eventually, the Bensons moved on to their third Burger yacht, a 122-footer, while Lady Grace Marie was reportedly sold to a media publisher. The third and the fourth owners were both Burger Yacht connoisseurs. The fourth one, who renamed the 1998 yacht Silver Seas, as it’s known today, was the one who changed its destiny by investing wholeheartedly in a major refit, something that few yacht owners are generally willing to do,
At the time, Silver Seas had already two decades of cruising under its belt, and a comprehensive refit was needed for sure. The operation took several years, and some experts in the industry considered more of a reconstruction than a standard refit. The hull was refaired before the full paint job, all windows were reinstalled, all the interior woodwork was refreshed with new varnish, and new marble tile was installed throughout.
Photo: IYC A major overhaul of both engines was one of the most important parts of the refit, along with the addition of new electronics, new premium appliances for the galley, new carpeting, flooring, and water toys. Practically, almost everything was brand-new, ensuring a prosperous future for the late ‘90s yacht. Although this was a multi-million-dollar investment for the owner (added to what he had paid for the yacht itself), the newly-upgraded Silver Seas was never expensive.
When it was still valued at almost $6 million, brokers said that this was one-third of the reconstruction cost alone. This year, Silver Seas’ price dropped even lower, until it eventually found its new owner, someone who was lucky enough to get a beautiful 107-footer with the glorious Burger DNA and the condition of a brand-new yacht (meaning no more investments from his part would be needed).
Today, almost three decades after its famous debut, Silver Seas is still one of the finest examples of an American-built raised-pilothouse yacht below 50 meters. Tri-deck superyachts became almost ubiquitous in the 2000s, replacing the raised-pilothouse yachts of what is now a gone era.
As the name suggests, Silver Seas’ raised pilothouse sits several steps from the main level, boasting a spacious layout and expansive views, thanks to five canted windshields forward, plus two large windows on each side. Honey teak panels cover this classic pilothouse throughout, and generous seating allows guests to enjoy the view, without disturbing the helmsman.
Photo: IYC Technology-wise, this raised pilothouse provides upgraded navigation systems for safer and more comfortable cruising, including a couple of proprietary Burger systems for multiple function monitoring, and a night-vision camera.
In terms of accommodation, this 107-footer welcomes up to eight guests across four elegant staterooms. The master suite is located forward, with easy access from the lower foyer, and all the three guest cabins are located to port. All have private en-suites, cedar closets, and individual temperature controls.
Twin MTU engines allows comfortable cruising 16 knots (with a maximum speed of 20 knots). Just like in its original days, this almost 30-year-old yacht is still well-appointed for comfortable, extended vacations in the Bahamas and the Caribbean – the favorite playgrounds of many US millionaires.
As the biggest Burger built before the 2000s era, and the only one today with an open flybridge and raised pilothouse, Silver Seas enjoys an iconic status (although not reflected in the modest $4.9 million price tag). Sold to a new owner, it will continue to operate under a different name, but with the same DNA and instantly recognizable pastel blue hull.
Photo: IYC Burger Yachts, founded in 1863 in Manitowoc, Wisconsin, is not only one of the most important names in America’s yacht-building history, but also one of the oldest yacht builders in the world.
To own any Burger yacht is something to be proud of, and we should all be especially thankful to owners like Silver Seas’ previous owner, who are willing and happy to pump money into a Burger yacht just to ensure it will stay in shape for many more decades – that is how the legend lives on.

This French Gem Is a Different Kind of Beach Tiny House with a Secret Perk
22 photos
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof
Close enough to the ocean to be a beach house, yet wonderfully hidden among trees and bushes, this unique house on wheels is a wonderland waiting to be discovered.
Apparently plain, yet delightfully mysterious, this French tiny house doesn’t have a fancy name. It’s simply referred to as “The Tiny” (La Tiny), in order to differentiate it from the other houses on the same property, all operating under the new Kof Ha Kof brand, and all equally whimsical.
Located less than ten minutes away (by foot) from the rugged beaches of Kreac’h and Bassinic, in Brittany, but also comfortably close to a hiking trail, The Tiny is a beach house with a twist, perfect for outdoor enthusiasts who want to explore as many adventures as possible. Close enough to the ocean for its guests to feel the breeze in the air, The Tiny was specifically nestled in a romantic grove, for full privacy and no overlooking neighbors.
At the same time, this isn’t a rugged, isolated haven built for an extreme off-grid experience. The abode itself shares the same property as the bigger and smaller hospitality units operated by Kof Ha Kof, and is also less than 2 km (1.2 miles) away from the small town of Plouguerneau, with bars, restaurants, and of course, the famous French bakeries.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof The Tiny is a private sanctuary and a trendy vacation home at the same time. A perfect choice for those who want to be near the beach, it’s also secluded and peaceful enough for intense creative activity of any kind, and writing in particular. In fact, writers were some of the main types of guests that the hosts had in mind when they added this tiny abode to their property.
The house is brand-new. It was delivered this past summer, by La Tiny House, one of the oldest and most reputable tiny house builders in France. They operate a workshop near the famous Mont-Saint-Michel, and their roots go back to more than ten years ago, when the original co-founders built the first two tiny homes in France. Those pioneering dwellings were followed by more than 30 tiny homes completed by 2016.
Since then, La Tiny House has continued to create and build custom homes on wheels with wooden frames, timber claddings, and natural interiors. Artisan craftsmanship took some of the most diverse, quirky shapes, in the hands of this team, and smart layouts were always topped with unusual, but very clever solutions for enhanced functionality.
The custom tiny house built for Kof Ha Kof had to check certain boxes, such as wide openings, a spacious covered terrace, a bespoke bookcase, and a suspended desk. It also had to be an eco-friendly, sustainable abode in two ways, both in terms of the materials used for its construction and furniture, and in terms of how it would integrate into the natural environment.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof Folks at Kof Ha Kof see the beautiful location of their hospitality units as a true paradise on earth that needs to be cherished and protected, not just enjoyed. This also implies encouraging guests to lean toward a more sustainable lifestyle even during their short stay, by using minimal heat for instance (the tiny house was particularly well-insulated precisely for lower energy needs), even though they still have access to Wi-Fi and a TV.
The suspended desk is the unexpected perk that makes this beach tiny house extra-special. More often seen in Australian and Kiwi homes on wheels, this desk concept turns a loft into a multi-purpose space that is more than a bedroom. The main advantage is, of course, space efficiency – when there’s no room downstairs for a classic home office or even a tiny desk, a suspended desk turns the loft into an unconventional office space that still remains a bedroom.
For this particular tiny house, the builder cleverly placed this suspended desk at the outer edge of the loft, not in the back (which is another possible placement, in front of a window). It might seem a bit weird and uncomfortable to let your legs hang in the air while sitting at this quirky desk, but it’s a proven, and popular alternative to classic home offices. Plus, you get the benefit of an expansive view of the entire house, with windows that draw the eye outside.
Especially if you’re a writer, you’d love this tiny, but whimsical space dedicated to your creativity. And there’s more. Downstairs, guests have access to a fully-equipped, rustic-style kitchen, a simple but beautifully-styled bathroom, and a lounge that truly feels like an oasis within an oasis.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof This lounge takes up a big chunk of the floor space, and it’s the first thing you see when you step inside the tiny house. Some might recognize classic features of the popular Nordic style, such as the huge picture window, the natural wood details, and the overall peaceful, dreamy ambiance. However, the builder made this part of the house even better by adding a second, asymmetric window above the oversized one (similar to a classic transom window).
This second window doesn’t just bring in a lot more natural light, but also draws the eye upward and outside – a small, but effective optical illusion that makes a living place seem much more spacious. An elegant L-shaped sofa is the heart and soul of this bright, airy lounge. It offers both comfy seating (with colorful cushions on top of the bespoke upholstery) and generous storage inside its wide, open shelves.
Even the coffee table is a piece of artisan craftsmanship, similar to a vintage treasure chest but also built with open shelves for extra storage space. Colorful artwork, one of the signature features of this French hospitality brand, adorns the lounge and even the kitchen area, adding both a touch of vibrant color and a bit of whimsy.
The built-in bookcase shelves, one of the main requests for this tiny house, sit elegantly above the sofa – big enough to display plenty of books (another signature addition you’ll find in evert Kof Ha Kof abode) but discreet enough to fit with the rest of the furniture, without looking bulky.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof Although compact, the kitchen could very well find its way in any French tiny house intended for full-time accommodation. It has a full-size oven and a small fridge, both tucked under the countertop, a compact induction stove, and a small sink. An open-shelf pantry sitting right between the kitchen and the bathroom provides added storage space for appliances and cleaning supplies.
Instead of bulky upper cupboards, this bright and colorful kitchen has just a couple of dainty shelves and a tiny cupboard mounted on the wall, in addition to the custom-crafted lower cabinets with pigeon hole-style designs.
There’s also a lovely breakfast bar facing the kitchen, cleverly placed under a big window. With two simple chairs, it becomes the perfect dining area for two, complete with whimsical tableware provided by the hosts.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof Guests also have the wonderful option to dine outside, on the beautiful deck. It’s covered, which means it can be enjoyed any time of the day and in any weather, and it’s a lot bigger than you’d expect: nine square meters (just under 97 square feet).
Envisioned as a beautiful private sanctuary for writers and other creative souls, The Tiny is ultimately a beach house sprinkled with French charm and the revitalizing power of a natural environment.

Toyota Cuts Tacoma's Free Maintenance in Half for Model Year 2027
17 photos
Photo: Toyota
Under the 2026 model year ToyotaCare plan for the Tacoma, the mid-size pickup enjoyed factory-scheduled maintenance for two years or 25,000 miles, whichever comes first. Upgrading to the 2027 model is actually a downgrade from this point of view, for Toyota Motor North America has reduced coverage to one year or 10,000 miles. In other words, two instead of four potential complimentary visits.
A substantial reduction, for sure, but what rattles me is how Toyota's announcement makes a poor effort to communicate it. The media release detailing the 2027 model year Tacoma for the US market spends page after page explaining new convenience features, off-road equipment, and infotainment stuff. Only at the end of said release, the maintenance plan gets a single sentence.
One sentence, yes, and Toyota Motor North America couldn't be bothered to explain this reduction.
More curiously, TMNA didn't even compare it with the outgoing arrangement or flag it among the headline changes for 2027. While the manufacturer cannot be accused of concealing the new coverage, stripping the relevant numbers of the context needed to understand what customers are losing isn't a good look at all.
The downgrade becomes more evident when the actual mileage schedule is considered. Toyota recommends scheduling maintenance every 5,000 miles or six months, with routine visits including fluid level checks, tire rotations, and inspections of the chassis, brakes, and wipers. Oil and filter replacement is recommended every 10,000 miles or 12 months under normal driving conditions.
Under the 2026 model year ToyotaCare arrangement for the US market, customers who followed the calendar-based schedule could receive up to four services over two years. The new plan covers two. Adding insult to injury, the general ToyotaCare brochure illustrates an oil and filter change at six and 12 months even though its footnote informs customers that service requirements vary by model.
Photo: Toyota Removing the 24-month visit from the complimentary period means that customers lose the second normally scheduled oil and filter replacement. If you're good at math, you might have also noticed that the mileage allowance has fallen by 60 rather than 50 percent. Toyota 's presentation of the change makes it all the more irritating.
The Japanese automaker cites customer feedback when explaining why the 14-inch media system is being made easier to configure, then describes revised packaging as a value improvement. Yet it offers no comparable explanation for removing a year and 15,000 miles of scheduled maintenance. What gives?
Toyota Motor North America is offsetting costs this way, namely production and tariff costs. As you're well aware, all Tacos produced for model year 2027 hail from Mexico. That means all 2027 models are tariffed at 25 percent under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, and this levy eats into Toyota's margin.
Absorbing the tariff, therefore, can be considered a major driver behind the ToyotaCare downgrade. Even so, we also have to consider parts and labor inflation. That being said, imagine saving $250 per truck in dealer reimbursements by cutting three dealership visits. $250 times 274,638 Tacomas delivered in the US last year is a lot of money, and it's rather pitiful that it has come to this.

Lawmakers in Italy are paving the way to again have nuclear power as part of the country’s energy mix. Legislators in Italy’s Senate in September approved a measure that supports Premier Giorgia Meloni’s drive to meet climate goals and bolster energy security. Officials have acknowledged that construction of new reactors is likely still several years away, but said the bill is important because it establishes a legal framework to pursue next-generation nuclear technologies. The legislation authorizes the government to draft implementing decrees over the next year that would look at safety standards and licensing of new reactors, and provide guidance for waste management. It also would set the criteria needed to choose the sites of new nuclear power plants.
A public referendum 1987 led Italy to move away from nuclear power following the 1986 Chernobyl disaster. The country closed its last nuclear power stations in 1990. Government officials in 2008 said they wanted to revive nuclear power, and then-Minister of Economic Development Claudio Scajola made a proposal to build up to 10 new reactors by 2030. That plan met opposition after the 2011 Fukushima incident in Japan, and voters in Italy later that year overwhelmingly said they supported a ban on nuclear construction.
Meloni’s government, though, has revived the discussion around nuclear power, with a particular focus on small modular reactors (SMRs). Gilberto Pichetto Fratin, the country’s minister of the Environment and Energy Security, after the September approval said, “Today, Italy is taking a step toward the future: the approval of the government’s mandate for new, sustainable nuclear power completes a process begun three years ago, aimed at exploring the potential of this new, clean, and sustainable technology. Nuclear power is not a return to the past: it is a winning technology, which, when integrated with renewables, can deliver extraordinary results for our energy security, toward neutrality by 2050.”
U.S. officials also are talking with counterparts in Italy about the country’s restart of nuclear power. Vannia Gava, Italy’s deputy minister for Environment and Energy Security, met recently with Jarrod Agen, executive director of the White House National Energy Dominance Council, during an official visit to Washington, D.C. “With Jarrod Agen, we shared at the White House a perspective that unites Italy and the United States: energy security is national security,” Gava said. “For manufacturing countries like Italy and the United States, this means ensuring reliable energy at affordable costs for businesses, diversifying sources, including next-generation nuclear power in the energy mix, and choosing stable and reliable partners.”
Nuward, a French company and a subsidiary of multinational energy company EDF, plus Edison and Italian industrial partners Ansaldo and Maire, earlier this year stressed their “common vision for the development of small modular reactors (SMRs) in Europe and their ambition to deploy a first reactor in Italy by 2035.” Newcleo, a France-headquartered developer of lead-cooled advanced modular reactors, also has considerable operations in Italy, including the first non-nuclear precursor prototype of its lead-cooled fast reactor. Last year it signed a memorandum of understanding with Italian cement association Federbeton to assess the potential for Newcleo’s technologies to work with the cement industry. Nuward recently said it wants to have a fleet of 10 of its SMRs across five European Union (EU) member countries, with initial construction beginning in 2030. Nuward in a statement posted on social media wrote, “Beyond the deployment of a first reactor, this momentum creates tangible opportunities for Italian industry to contribute to the development of the technology and become part of the value chain of the future European #SMR programme.”
1. This is a conceptual rendering that illustrates the integration of Terra Innovatum’s SOLO Micro-Modular Nuclear Reactor into an industrial complex, where it would provide electricity and thermal energy through cogeneration. Courtesy: Terra Innovatum Global N.V
Italy-headquartered Terra Innovatum Global N.V. , which has developed the SOLO Micro-Modular Reactor (Figure 1), is among the groups that support the country’s return to nuclear power. “Today represents an important milestone for Italy and for the broader European nuclear industry,” said Alessandro Petruzzi, co-founder and CEO of Terra Innovatum, after the move by the country’s lawmakers in September. “Italy has remained an important contributor to the nuclear supply chains of both Europe and the United States, with extraordinary capabilities across nuclear engineering, advanced manufacturing, and energy infrastructure. The decision to create a pathway for the return of nuclear energy recognizes the increasingly important role advanced nuclear technologies can play in providing reliable, carbon-free power.”
Terra Innovatum made a presentation about its SOLO technology during the 70th International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) General Conference in Vienna, Austria, in September. Company officials have said they think smaller, modular, factory-manufactured reactors such as SOLO can expand nuclear energy beyond traditional large-scale power plants. Terra Innovatum is developing the SOLO micro-modular reactor around proven nuclear technologies. It would use low-enriched uranium fuel.
“As Italy advances its new nuclear framework, the distinction between technologies in R&D [research and development] and those approaching commercial deployment will become increasingly important,” said Giordano Morichi, founding partner and managing director of Global Business Development and Investor Relations for Terra Innovatum. “SOLO was engineered for commercialization, with approximately $4 billion in pre-commercial commitments across data centers, industrial projects, and other energy-intensive applications globally.”
Dr. Massimo Morichi, Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) for Terra Innovatum, told POWER that the government’s decision “reflects a reassessment of Italy’s long-term energy needs rather than a single political or technological breakthrough. Meloni has presented nuclear power as a means of strengthening national energy security, while Fratin has argued that it could contribute to a more balanced and competitive energy mix. The government’s longer-term ambition is to integrate nuclear generation into Italy’s decarbonization strategy.”
The CSO said there is also a “significant industrial dimension. Italy retains nuclear engineering, manufacturing, research, and decommissioning capabilities despite having no operating commercial nuclear power plants. Building on this established expertise, a new program could create further opportunities for domestic suppliers, engineering companies, and research institutions, while strengthening Italy’s positioning as a key industrial player in the international market for advanced reactors. The timing is very significant because nuclear technologies are evolving, European countries are reconsidering their energy strategies, and modular reactor designs are attracting renewed investment. Italy is seeking to establish a framework now so that it can participate in this emerging market rather than remain dependent on technologies developed elsewhere.”
Terra Innovatum is advancing SOLO through the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing process. The company, pending regulatory approvals, is targeting first-of-its-kind deployment next year, with commercial deployment and scale-up by the end of 2028.
Morichi said, “Italy must also distinguish between the cost of building a reactor and the cost of the electricity it produces over its lifetime. A smaller project may require less capital overall but can have a higher cost per megawatt than a successfully delivered large plant. The promised economic advantages therefore depend on execution and repeat deployment, not just reactor size. For Italy, the attraction is not simply to build smaller reactors, it is to establish a repeatable model that could support a broader nuclear program while limiting the financial and construction risks associated with each individual project.”
Gava at the meeting with Agen said the U.S. and Italy also have talked about addressing vulnerabilities in supply chains for the energy sector, in addition to collaborating on nuclear power. “During our discussion, we focused on critical raw materials, on which energy security will increasingly depend in the coming years, and whose refining is currently concentrated in very few countries,” said Gava. “This is a vulnerability that the West must address together, building shared supply chains and partnerships with producing countries.”
Gava highlighted Italy’s critical minerals agreement with the U.S., noting it could strengthen the Italian government’s role in the Pax Silica initiative, a U.S.-led project launched in December of last year. Officials said the strategy is designed to build a resilient, allied economic consensus around artificial intelligence, semiconductors, and critical mineral supply chains. The EU already has selected five Italy-led projects focused on critical materials processing and recycling.
—Darrell Proctor is a senior editor for POWER.

Zeekr officially unveiled the 7X at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show. The model launches with a promotional starting price of roughly $32,000. For the money, customers get the refreshed mid-size electric SUV sitting on a 900-volt architecture, a new battery option, and a hardware upgrade across all trims.
The entire Zeekr 7X lineup is now underpinned by the new 900-volt high-voltage platform. A new 85-kWh Energee Golden Brick LFP battery pack joins the 7X lineup, offering 5.5C charging support, recharging from 10% to 8% in roughly 10.5 minutes.
At the top of the lineup sits the dual-motor Ultra variant with a dual-motor powertrain, producing 785 horsepower (795 metric horsepower) and 599 pound-feet (812 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make it rocket from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 2.98 seconds, which basically places the midsize SUV in the supercar territory.
The all-new 7X debuts the Qianli Haohan G-ASD 4.1 driver assistance system, powered by 31 perception sensors, including standard LiDAR. The SUV also gets the Super Eva AI assistant alongside front-row zero-gravity seats with 12 massage points and eight massage modes.
Photo: Zeekr Cloud Comfort seats, with a 134-degree recline angle and 8.46 inches (215 millimeters) of power sliding travel, heating and pneumatic massage, are in the second row for luxury sedan-like comfort.
Regardless of the trim, the X7 features a standard high-speed tire blowout stabilization system, which keeps the vehicle traveling straight and prevents rollovers or spins if a tire suddenly bursts at highway speed.
All trims also feature Continuously Controlled Damping (CCD) electromagnetic damping, the adaptive suspension technology that adjusts the firmness of a vehicle's shock absorbers in real time. The active road noise cancelation with laminated acoustic glass across all four doors is also on the menu.
Zeekr is selling the X7 in three distinct variants. The X7 RWD Max with the 75 kWh battery pack and 385 miles (620 kilometers) of range sits at the base of the lineup. Higher in the range is the RWD Max+ with the 85 kWh battery pack and 423 miles (680 kilometers) of range.
Photo: Zeekr This variant can also be ordered with the larger 103 kWh CATL Qilin battery, which takes the range all the way to 498 miles (802 kilometers). The same battery pack equips the AWD Ultra, but this variant can drive as far as 444 miles (715 kilometers) before it needs to be plugged in again.
Zeekr launched the all-new 7X with a promotional price starting at 216,800 yuan, which translates to roughly $32,400, instead of the usual 229,800 yuan ($34,300). The range-topping AWD Ultra is a 269,800-yuan ($40,300) deal.

Photo: © Makidotvn
By Charlotte Goldstone
27 November 2026
Air cargo rates continue to face upward pressure as capacity constraints, rather than a surge in peak season demand, increasingly dictate pricing – with freighter capacity into Europe taking a significant hit ahead of Black Friday.
Data published today by aviation consultant Aevean shows freighter capacity from Asia and the Middle East into Europe fell 15% year on year in the two weeks to 24 November, equivalent to some 27,500 tonnes.
“Black Friday… or Red Friday?” asked Maarten Wormer, head of consulting at Aevean, noting that “integrator and general cargo hubs are largely holding up, as ecommerce gateways take the hit”.
Budapest recorded the steepest percentage decline among the eight major gateways tracked, at 36%, followed by Paris CDG, down 27%, and Liège, down 24% – the latter losing some 5,800 tonnes of capacity.
Meanwhile, Frankfurt saw an 11% reduction, while Cologne bucked the trend with a 16% increase. Capacity into Amsterdam remained flat.
The figures come amid a resurgence in global airfreight rates, following a period of easing in the third quarter.
According to Transport Intelligence’s (Ti) latest Air Freight Rate Tracker, global headhaul rates reached $3.92 per kg in early November, up 7.6% on October, 8.7% against the Q3 average, and 45.2% year on year.
Backhaul rates climbed 6.2% month on month, to $3 per kg, up 22.3% year on year.
However, it is the withdrawal of bellyhold capacity during winter passenger schedules, coupled with persistently high fuel costs, rather than exceptional demand growth, that Ti identified as driving the increases.
Westbound transatlantic rates recorded the largest quarterly increase, at 21.7%, largely reflecting seasonal capacity reductions.
But technology shipments continue to underpin demand elsewhere, with South Asia-North America remaining the most expensive tradelane tracked by Ti, at $7.08 per kg, up 70.5% year on year. And the strength of demand for AI infrastructure, servers and semiconductors could see freighters redeployed to the Transpacific, further tightening capacity elsewhere.
Meanwhile, there is little consensus over whether shippers can expect much respite in the new year.
Despite 72% of respondents to Ti’s industry survey anticipating rate increases over the next three months, the consultant expects prices to ease in Q1 27, recalling that rates fell between Q4 and Q1 in each of the past four years.
Some 81% of respondents expected increases on the Asia-US West Coast trade.
While softer e-commerce, consumer, and industrial demand following the peak season should weigh on pricing, sustained technology shipments and limited capacity are expected to cushion any decline.
Ti also suggested shippers should avoid locking-in November rates on 12-month contracts – shorter-term agreements or index-linked pricing potentially offering greater flexibility.
And Transatlantic shippers could benefit from delaying tenders until the return of summer passenger schedules in late March, when the additional bellyhold capacity could bring some relief.

Rossinavi's New Alfa Superyacht Boasts Sporty Styling and an Automotive-Inspired Bow Shield
8 photos
Photo: Rossinavi
There is nothing that screams luxury more than a custom superyacht. Designed as floating sanctuaries with every detail, from the naval architecture to interior materials and onboard amenities, dictated by the owner, bespoke superyachts are the ultimate expression of luxury on the open seas.
One of the leading shipyards known for turning bold visions into reality is Rossinavi, and the 62-meter (203-foot) full-custom Alfa superyacht is a great example of the Italian shipyard’s exceptional nautical craftsmanship.
Alfa is the latest custom creation launched by Rossinavi at its facilities in Viareggio and is the result of a collective effort between Fulvio De Simoni Yacht Design, which penned the exterior, Arrabito Naval Architect, which took care of naval architecture, and Omega Interior Design and Architecture for the interior.
Created as a one-off project for a client represented by Karma Yachting throughout the construction process, the vessel hit the water on November 25. It’s a full-displacement superyacht with a steel hull and aluminum superstructure that combines a sporty exterior with generous outdoor spaces, and a layout designed around privacy and onboard comfort.
Photo: Rossinavi Rossinavi is known for blending Italian naval architecture and interior craftsmanship with bold exterior lines, frequently drawing inspiration from automotive design, and this is also the case with Alfa. The vessel stands out with a sporty silhouette with dynamic lines, but its defining feature is an automotive-inspired bow shield, which incorporates a pronounced ridge and lights. Apart from acting as a starting point for the sporty appearance, it also gives the forward section of the yacht a truly distinctive look.
Like a true contemporary yacht, Alfa features ample glazing surfaces, but the windows on its lower and main decks feature a hull-colored treatment that makes the blend with the surrounding surface, creating the appearance of a continuous hull with no openings. The same approach to design consistency extends to the bulwarks, swimming pool, and outdoor furniture.
Another standout feature is the aft mezzanine deck, which acts as a link between the main and upper deck spaces while also shielding the main deck cockpit from the stern views and creating a sense of privacy. Designed to provide a seamless connection with the sea, the beach club opens through both aft and lateral openings, which connect with the swim platform to form a continuous space for spending time close to the water.
Photo: Rossinavi With a maximum beam of 11.1 meters (36.4 feet) and an interior volume of 1,210 GT, Alfa provides generous living quarters. It can accommodate up to 12 guests in six cabins, including two VIP cabins on the main deck and three guest staterooms below. Crew quarters provide space for 13 people across seven cabins.
The upper deck is home to a private owner’s apartment, which is designed as a retreat with its own outdoor area featuring a Jacuzzi, lounge seating and a sunbathing area. The sky lounge is a versatile space that can either remain part of the owner’s private quarters when desired or be opened for shared guest use on other occasions.
An al-fresco dining area on the same deck can be enclosed by sliding panels, transforming into a veranda with a dedicated heating and cooling system. This means it’s a space that can be enjoyed in any season.
Photo: Rossinavi Wellness facilities could not miss from a yacht designed for relaxation, entertainment, and comfort on the water. Alfa comes with several wellness amenities, including a massage room on the lower deck, a sauna near the beach club, and a gym at the aft end of the bridge deck. The custom yacht also has an observation deck, which offers another place for outdoor relaxation, with lounge seating, sunbathing areas, and panoramic views.
“The high standards of quality and design achieved with Alfa are the result of a close collaboration between Rossinavi and the Owner,” said Federico Rossi, Chief Operating Officer of Rossinavi. “From the very beginning, we have shared a common vision, working together to bring this project to life and achieve a result that reflects our mutual aspirations and expectations.”
Details regarding Alfa”s propulsion system and maximum and cruising speeds have not yet been disclosed. The superyacht’s delivery is scheduled for March 2027.

Hyundai unveiled the Mercury Concept, a preview of its upcoming entry-level electric SUV set to launch as the IONIQ M in 2027.
Meet the Hyundai Mercury EV Concept
Following the IONIQ V, which went on sale in September, Hyundai offered a look at its upcoming IONIQ lineup for China at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27.
Hyundai’s Mercury Concept stole the spotlight. The concept previews its upcoming “B-segment premium smart SUV,” set to launch in China in 2027.
According to Hyundai, the IONIQ M will be “the most accessible entry-level model in the IONIQ universe.” Unfortunately, it’s designed specifically for China.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Like the IONIQ V, the electric SUV was developed by Hyundai Motor’s Chinese design and engineering team. As such, it features a unique style and advanced tech you won’t find in Hyundai’s vehicles sold in the US, Europe, or other overseas markets.
The SUV’s futuristic low-slung design is inspired by Mercury’s orbit around the sun. Up front, the shark-nose design and slim, edgy lights form Hyundai’s “H” badge, while an integrated rear spoiler adds to the compact, sporty look.
Hyundai said the production version will feature Zhuoyu L2++ ADAS and a high-tech cabin powered by ByteDance’s Doubao AI model.
A battery-swap version is also set to launch through Hyundai’s partnership with China’s CATL following the production IONIQ M.
The IONIQ M joins Hyundai’s EV lineup in 2027
The Mercury follows the Venus, now on sale as the IONIQ V, and the larger Earth SUV, as Hyundai’s third IONIQ Planet name designed for China. It will go on sale in 2027 as the IONIQ M, alongside the IONIQ V EREV.
In 2028, Hyundai will launch the production version of the Earth SUV, while two new energy vehicles will join the lineup in 2029.
From left to right: Hyundai IONIQ V EREV, Mercury Concept, and Earth Concept (Source: Hyundai Motor)
While Hyundai didn’t reveal battery or powertrain specs, it will likely feature a similar setup to the IONIQ V.
The Hyundai IONIQ V is available in China with two CATL lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery packs: A 53.5 kWh battery paired with a 140 kW (188 hp) rear electric motor that offers a CLTC range of up to 540 km, or a 66.8 kWh battery paired with a 168 kW (225 hp) motor with a CLTC range of up to 650 km (404 miles).
Hyundai said the IONIQ M will be “the most accessible entry-level model in the IONIQ universe.” Given the IONIQ V starts at 109,900 yuan ($16,500), the production IONIQ M could be priced around 99,000 yuan ($15,000) in China.

There's a New Motorcycle Race Engine in Town, Triumph's Moto2 Triple Lands in 2027
38 photos
Photo: Triumph
After back in the scorching days of August, British bike maker Triumph let slip the first details on the new engine that will be used in the MotoGP Moto2 World Championship, it came back on the matter this week and fully revealed the changes it made. And let me tell you, there is plenty to talk about.
Triumph has been the sole engine supplier for Moto2 ever since 2019, and it has constantly improved the makeup and capabilities of the 765cc triple that was used in the bikes raced by young riders. What happens for the upcoming season, though, marks the biggest change made to it over the past seven years.
First up, the engine is now larger, having grown from 765cc to 798cc. This was achieved, among other things, by means of deploying a new crankshaft and a 2.25 mm longer stroke – the bore, however, stays put at 78 mm.
The Brits say they have completely redesigned the cylinder head, fitting it with a finger-follower valvetrain and titanium inlet valves. The inlet and exhaust valves are larger than they used to be, the intake ports have been redesigned, and there's a new, twin airbox that allows an increase of ten percent in airflow and more aggressive cam profiles.
Photo: Triumph Finally, Triumph's engineers installed new high-flow Bosch fuel injectors to improve fuel delivery and burn, and reimagined the combustion chamber that, together with the new pistons, increases the compression ratio from 13.5:1 to 14.0:1.
The engine also comes along with increased power levels (by that I mean both hp and torque) – not insanely larger, but still large enough to make a difference on the tracks, in the heat of the race, for talented riders.
In its current form, the Triumph Moto2 powerplant is rated at 128 horsepower, but the new 2027 unit takes that higher by some six percent – that would translate to a max horsepower level of 136 hp.
When it comes to torque, Triumph worked its magic and now says that the engine delivers more of it throughout the rev range - speaking of that, the powerplant's max rev sits at an impressive 13,800 rpm.
Photo: Triumph To accommodate the changes made to the powerplant, Triumph also had to make some upgrades to the things that tie into it, including the primary drive and the transmission. Sadly, we're not told exactly what those changes are.
Finally, there is also talk of the engine as a whole dropping some of its weight, thanks to the lighter cylinder head, for instance – the larger-displacement powerplant tips the scales almost five pounds (2.2 pounds) faster than the one it replaces.
We're told the upgrades mentioned above have not been implemented on a whim, but as a result of data gathered over some 1.2 million miles (two million km) of travel from riders that climbed not only on the back of the Moto2 race bikes, but also the other two-wheelers that carry this kind of powerplant in their frames, like the Street Triple 765 RS.
Triumph is now getting ready to start official testing of the powerplant ahead of the 2027 Moto2 season opener in March. In some way, though, that has been happening for a while now, as the new engine will require new chassis to support it, on account of the changes made to the air intake position and engine mounting points. According to the Brits, manufacturers have been testing solutions to those upgrades for about a year now.
Photo: Triumph The engine Triumph has been supplying Moto2 rides with has more than proven its worth on the track, even if, technically speaking, it is only competing against itself. We're told that in the eight years or so it has been raced, the triple has been responsible for setting no less than 89 all-time records and 77 race records. Of that, no less than 37 were achieved in 2025.
To mark the launch of the new Moto2 race engine, which is expected not only to follow in the footsteps of its predecessor, but also surpass it, Triumph released on the same day the details of the powerplant of a motorcycle that's meant to honor it. They call it Street Triple 798 Moto2 Edition , and it builds on the previously unveiled Street Triple 798 RS.
Packing the same displacement engine that'll go into the Moto2 racers, the bike is one of the lightest around, tipping the scales at 399 pounds (181 kg, wet weight). There will only be 1,000 units of this motorcycle made, evenly divided into two body colors, and each of them sells for $17,295. These bikes should be on the roads by May 2027.
We will keep an eye on what comes next for the new race engine and report back when something new comes along. In the meantime, you can enjoy the way it looks in the attached gallery, where it's shown both on its own and installed in the frame of the Moto2 Edition.

By Alex Lennane
27 November 2026
WiseTech Global has offered 16 major CargoWise customers an early move to its new pricing model, opening the way for it to charge for AI-driven labour savings. One has already signed, the company told shareholders at its AGM on Friday.
WiseTech is starting with the 20 largest customers still on long-term contracts under its previous pricing model. This group represents just 3.7% of CargoWise customers but about 28% of its revenue, based on H1 FY26 figures. They are due to move automatically to CargoWise Value Packs when their deals expire, with about three-quarters of those contracts due to end by FY29.
“We expect initial revenue on conversion to be neutral for us,” said CEO Zubin Appoo. Moving to Value Packs unlocks access to CargoWise’s AI agents, and WiseTech expects to earn more as customers meet agreed milestones for labour savings and efficiency. Co-founder Richard White said the company intended to charge “a tiny fraction of that labour saving”.
WiseTech illustrated the potential with a calculation based on published staff costs. A 10% reduction could save some large forwarders US$180m-$300m a year, it said. The company did not disclose how it would measure savings for billing, or what share it would charge. It now has nine CargoWise AI agents live, up from six in August, with three more in pilot.
Among the forwarders to watch is DSV. In September, Mr Appoo told The Loadstar WiseTech had discussed moving DSV onto Value Packs before its contract expires in September 2028. DSV chief executive Jens Lund said he expected CargoWise and Tango, the forwarding platform DSV inherited from Schenker, to run alongside each other for some time. WiseTech did not name the customer that had already signed, or say whether DSV was among the 16.
Despite a growing choice of forwarding software, and fears that competition would stymie CargoWise’s ability to attract new customers, it is still winning new business. WiseTech reported some 30% more new CargoWise signings in the first ten months this year than in the same period last year, with signings among small and medium-sized businesses up about 40%.
CargoWise revenue also rose 11% year on year in the four months to October, helped by higher transaction volumes, growth from large global forwarders, and price increases on legacy contracts.
WiseTech, which said its e2open integration is ahead of schedule, held its FY27 revenue guidance at US$1.48bn–$1.54bn. CFO Jeff Howard said trading to October gave the company confidence it could reach US$1.48bn–$1.5bn if momentum and favourable market conditions continued, before factoring-in uptake of early Value Pack conversions, paid AI features, and its VerifyWise supplier verification service.
Shareholder case and competition inquiry continue
WiseTech also said the Australian Federal Police had closed its investigation into founder Mr White without taking action. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission has also closed its governance inquiry without enforcement action, and issued no-action letters to Mr White and two employees in a separate share-trading inquiry. The inquiry into alleged trading by a fourth individual continues.
Meanwhile, the company noted that the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission’s investigation into the supply of global logistics services and software remained at an early stage.
WiseTech is also defending a shareholder class action in the Supreme Court of Victoria. Investors allege the company misled the market and breached its disclosure obligations over expected earnings and potential acquisition payments in 2019 and 2020.
WiseTech cut about 1,700 roles in FY26, mainly in product development and customer service. Its October employee survey put engagement at 68%, down from 76% in February 2025.

BMW M3 Electric Spied on Video in the Open, Neue Klasse Model Expected in 2027
6 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | PrototypeHunters
BMW continues to tap deeper into the electric game, and one of the upcoming models that will feature a zero-emission powertrain will be the M3 .
Mind you, one should not mistake it for the next-gen ICE-powered BMW M3, which will sit at the very top of the new-gen G5X lineup, utilizing an updated version of the CLAR platform. That’s because the first-ever BMW M3 Electric will be the range-topping version of the new i3, and it is based on the same Neue Klasse architecture.
The model will look very similar to its gasoline-fed sibling, as both feature influences from the BMW M Concept Neue Klasse . Nevertheless, that does not mean that the body panels will fit both models, as these will be different. After all, we are talking about vehicles based on different constructions, and with completely different powertrains.
We have encountered the BMW M3 Electric on numerous occasions over the last few months, with the prototypes gradually adding their final bits and pieces ahead of the production kick off. The video embedded at the bottom of the page puts the spotlight on several testers, revealing how they have evolved with each passing encounter, with an obvious emphasis on some of the details inside and out.

U.S. rail traffic rose 4.7% for the week ending November 21 from a year ago, the Association of American Railroads said, as intermodal volume again drove gains.
Containers and trailers improved 8.3% compared with the same week in 2025, while commodity carloads edged up 0.5%.
(Chart: AAR)
Six of the 10 carload commodity groups posted gains. Metallic ores and metals used in steelmaking led at 17.9%. Forest products rose 11% despite real estate market issues; petroleum and petroleum products improved 11.2%, and motor vehicles and parts rose 8.3% as year-end sales promotions outweighed higher interest rates. Farm products excluding grain and food were up 6.2%, and chemicals increased 2.1%.
Four groups declined as grain fell 17.4%, the steepest drop. Coal was off 4.4%, while unspecified carloads were off 2.1%, and nonmetallic minerals such as sand and stone dropped 0.9%.
Through the first 46 weeks of 2026, total U.S. rail freight traffic is up 4% from last 2025. Carloads are better by 2.7% and intermodal units are up 5.1%. Among commodities, metallic ores and metals lead year-to-date at 9%, followed by grain at 8.7% and petroleum products at 7.9%. Coal is the only major group down year-to-date, at 1.6%.
Across nine reporting U.S., Canadian and Mexican railroads, North American carloads for the week slipped 0.3%, while intermodal was ahead 8.4%. Combined traffic gained by 4.2%. For the first 46 weeks of the year, combined North American volume is up 3.5% from 2025.
Why It Matters: Rail volumes point to uneven conditions. Strong intermodal growth, which is tied to consumer goods and retail logistics, suggests healthy import and holiday-season shipping demand. Gains in metals, autos and petroleum point to steady industrial activity, while weaker grain and coal volumes show agricultural and energy shipments may be softening.

PARIS — France kicked off an initiative with its defense industry to produce counter-drone systems, a new chapter in efforts to foster a local drone ecosystem through “pacts” with industry that bring together firms and military end users, cut procurement red tape and focus on fast contract delivery.
The new pact adds a counter-drone dimension to France’s existing drone pact and will run to the end of summer 2027, said Emmanuel Levacher, chairman of defense-industry association Gicat and the CEO of military vehicle maker Arquus.
“We then hope it will be renewed while incorporating both drone and counter-drone, the idea being that one does not go without the other,” Levacher told Defense News on Wednesday night, after a presentation of the new counter-drone pact in the offices of semiconductor maker STMicroelectronics, just outside Paris.
The drone pact announced in June 2024 has been an attempt by France to play catch up in tactical drones and loitering munitions, led by the country’s Directorate General for Armament together with Gicat. Following up on the success of the original drone pact, France in November announced a similar pact for naval drones , on the occasion of the Euronaval defense trade show.
The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have been a “quite brutal reality check,” and French forces have an urgent need for counter-drone capabilities, Alice Rufo, France’s junior minister for the armed forces, said in a speech at the presentation. She said France has already faced problems related to having insufficient counter-drone capability, without providing details.
France has faced multiple incidents with drones overflying sensitive military sites, including the Île Longue nuclear submarine base in December 2025 and the Toulon naval base in October this year. French media have also reported drones flying over a Eurenco explosives plant in Bergerac and a freight train carrying Leclerc main battle tanks near Mulhouse in November 2025.
The new pact covers systems to counter unmanned aerial vehicles but also maritime and ground drones, according to Levacher. The Gicat chairman said he expects most or all of the 200 partners in the drone pact to participate in the counter-drone initiative.
The goal of the counter-drone pact is “to really be in contact with the armed forces” to understand their requirements, as well as with the DGA to facilitate testing, validation and orders, Levacher said.
“The idea is really to bring together all the stakeholders to create this cross-pollination, speed, contacts,” Levacher said. “This pact is a way of saying that this is an area that does still need to structure and organize itself a little.”
The drone pact has functioned as a meeting place for industry where companies have been able to find project partners, as well as a forum to share feedback from Ukraine, according to Levacher. The DGA uses the drone pact as a framework for informal calls for ideas.
While the demand, the connections and the ecosystem are primarily French, the drone pact firms also pursue export opportunities, Levacher said.
Within the framework of the drone pact, French startup Harmattan AI won a contract in June 2025 to supply the French Army with 1,000 low-cost drones, which it delivered in January this year ahead of the Orion exercise.

ROME — Italian defense giant Leonardo has rolled out the first of 15 M-346 jets due to take over stunt flying duties with the Italian Air Force’s aerobatic team.
Built as a jet trainer and also sold in a light fighter configuration, the M-346 jets configured for display team flying will be delivered to the Frecce Tricolori team between 2027 and 2028, Leonardo said in a statement.
The aircraft will replace the MB-339 PAN aircraft which has flown for more than 40 years, allowing for better aerobatic displays thanks to the M-346’s greater maneuverability, Leonardo said.
“The M-346 is now well positioned to pursue major new commercial and industrial cooperation opportunities worldwide, both as a trainer and multirole aircraft and as a platform for aerobatic teams,” said Stefano Bortoli, managing director of Leonardo’s Aircraft Division.
The new jets will be upgraded for the job with a smoke generation system, video streaming capabilities, avionics modifications and auxiliary fuel tanks.
Leonardo has now sold over 170 M-346 jets to 10 countries, with Italy, the Republic of Singapore, Israel, Poland, Qatar and Greece among customers for the trainer version.
The light fighter version has been sold to Turkmenistan, Nigeria, Austria and most recently Indonesia.
The M-346 F “Block 20” light fighter configuration comes with a Large Area Display (LAD), active electronically scanned radar, a Link 16 data-link, electronic countermeasures, and new weapons systems.

E-bike battery safety standards that have largely been voluntary across the US are on the verge of becoming mandatory federal requirements, following the passage of a major piece of legislation in Congress.
The US Senate unanimously passed H.R. 973 , known as the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act, on November 19. The House previously passed the bill in April 2025 by a 365-42 vote. The legislation now heads to the president for a signature.
So what does that actually mean for e-bikes and their batteries?
The biggest change is that the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) would be required to turn three widely used UL safety standards into mandatory federal consumer product safety standards. Those include UL 2271 for light electric vehicle batteries, UL 2849 for e-bike electrical systems, and UL 2272 for personal e-mobility devices such as electric scooters.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Currently, those standards are generally voluntary at the federal level, though some jurisdictions have already made them mandatory. New York City, for example, r equires certification to applicable UL standards for e-bikes, batteries, and other micromobility devices sold in the city.
If H.R. 973 becomes law, that approach would effectively go nationwide.
The bill gives the CPSC 180 days after enactment to promulgate the three standards as final consumer product safety standards. And this isn’t simply a one-time requirement based on today’s standards. Future revisions would generally become federal requirements 180 days after the CPSC is notified, unless the agency determines that a revision doesn’t improve safety.
What does this mean for the e-bike industry?
For established e-bike companies already selling UL-certified products, the immediate impact may be relatively small. Many major brands have already moved toward UL 2849 certification, particularly as retailers and municipalities have increasingly demanded it.
The bigger impact is likely to be felt at the lower end of the market, where inexpensive e-bikes, replacement batteries, and direct-import products have continued to enter the US without certification to recognized safety standards.
Importantly, UL certification isn’t a guarantee that a lithium-ion battery can never catch fire. Damage, improper repairs, incompatible chargers, manufacturing defects, and other problems can still create hazards.
But the standards are designed to test batteries and electrical systems against foreseeable electrical, mechanical, and environmental stresses. Making those standards mandatory would establish a nationwide minimum safety floor instead of leaving compliance largely voluntary.
I’d say that’s probably the biggest change here: we aren’t talking about a new e-bike technology or a new battery chemistry. We’re talking about taking safety standards that much of the reputable e-bike industry already follows and making them the baseline for everyone selling these products in America.

Elon Musk says Tesla’s cars don’t need the next-generation AI5 chip, so it’s going to Optimus first. A new report from Taiwan’s chip supply chain gives a more practical reason: Tesla won’t have enough AI5 chips for its cars until 2028.
According to Commercial Times , Tesla’s chip design partner Global Unichip (GUC) is giving its limited TSMC 3nm capacity for 2027 to Google and Microsoft data center chips first. That leaves Tesla with a relatively small AI5 allocation.
Musk: “Cars will remain at AI4”
Last Sunday, a Tesla owner asked Musk when AI5 would be in new cars. His answer: “It’s going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That’s enough to solve superhuman driving.”
As we reported this week, FSD v15 is basically AI4’s last shot . Tesla engineers are already squeezing the last few percent of utilization out of the chip, and the AI4.5 refresh is mostly a move to LPDDR5X memory. Musk said Tesla cut AI4.5 from 32GB to 24GB of RAM because “RAM is super expensive,” and that AI4 itself now costs twice as much due to memory and storage price hikes.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
It’s quite a change in plans. In June 2024, Musk said AI5 would be in vehicles in the second half of 2025. Tesla only taped out AI5 in April , and Musk had already started describing its focus as Optimus and Tesla’s supercomputer clusters.
Google and Microsoft get the 3nm wafers first
The Commercial Times report, published today, describes GUC as the custom ASIC design partner on Tesla’s AI5 project. GUC is the design services house whose largest shareholder is TSMC, and it works mostly on data center silicon.
Industry sources told the paper that GUC’s 2027 allocation of TSMC’s N3 capacity is much larger than this year’s. But with AI compute demand exploding, it still can’t serve every big customer at once.
So GUC is prioritizing North American cloud projects, including Google’s Axion 2 and Axion 3 server processors and Microsoft’s in-house chips. Those orders carry high margins and good visibility. Tesla’s robot and car chip doesn’t make the front of the line.
The result, according to the report, is that Tesla’s initial 2027 wafer quota can’t support annual shipments for a fleet of millions of cars. The supply chain expects that limited AI5 volume to go first to Optimus, which needs a lot of compute but ships in small numbers, and only expects large-scale adoption in cars after N3 capacity expands further in 2028.
TSMC is adding 3nm capacity, but not fast. Its new 3nm fab in Tainan is scheduled for volume production in the first half of 2027, and its second Arizona fab, which Musk has said will produce AI5, in the second half of 2027.
Samsung doesn’t fix 2027 either
Tesla does have a second source. Samsung is building its own version of AI5 on 2nm at its Taylor, Texas fab , but it expects volume production of Tesla’s AI chips there in the second half of 2027.
Now look at the numbers. Tesla delivered roughly 1.6 million vehicles last year. Every one of them needs a self-driving computer.
Optimus is a different story. Tesla now plans to put AI5 in Optimus around April 2027 and push external Optimus deliveries to late 2027 . Even an aggressive robot ramp next year is measured in thousands of units, not millions.
If your 2027 AI5 supply is a fraction of what a car program needs, Optimus is the only product Tesla has that can absorb it.
Electrek’s Take
Musk’s version is that cars don’t need AI5 because AI4 is “enough to solve superhuman driving.” The supply chain’s version is that Tesla can’t get enough AI5 chips to put in cars anyway. Both can be true at the same time, but only one of them explains the timing.
Look at how Tesla has been handling silicon this fall. It cut AI4.5 RAM. It cut AI5 RAM from 144GB to 72GB, then bumped it to 96GB a day later. It says AI4 costs double what it used to. That’s a company rationing chips and memory, not one choosing to leave a 12x compute upgrade on the shelf because it isn’t needed.
And if AI4 really were plenty, Tesla engineers wouldn’t be talking about squeezing out the last few percent of the chip for v15.
So here’s how we read it. Tesla had to pick where its scarce AI5 chips go in 2027, and it picked the low-volume product. “AI4 is enough” is the story that makes that decision sound like a choice. And it’s a story we heard about HW3, Tesla’s previous self-driving computer.

Why Is the Tesla Cybertruck Suddenly America's Fastest-Selling Used Pickup Truck?
66 photos
Photo: Tesla
Well, this is unexpected. Here we have an EV so commercially unsuccessful that its manufacturer announced it would discontinue production as early as next year. Yet, if you're a used car dealer in the United States, you might just want to stock up on Cybertrucks, as opposed to the always-popular Ford F-150.
According to a recent iSeeCars study, which looked at roughly 1.1 million used vehicle sales in October, the Cybertruck needed an average of just 39.1 days to find a new owner, compared to a whopping 65.5 days for the pickup truck segment as a whole. This is even more staggering when factoring in the fact that back in December of 2024, used Cybertrucks were spending roughly 75 days on dealer lots.
And no, Tesla hadn't yet announced they would be pulling the plug on the Cybertruck when the October 2026 data was first coming in. Otherwise, one could accuse people of simply rushing to get their hands on something that could one day become a collector's item. I mean, could it? I guess stranger things have happened.
So, what's so different about a used Cybertruck as opposed to a brand-new one? Aside from the pricing, of course - actually, it's not that big of a difference. Used models cost anywhere between 9% and 18% below MSRP, on average. Also, let's clarify again that we're talking about the Cybertruck becoming America's fastest-selling pickup truck, not its best-selling one. There's a considerable difference.
Here we go. I think there's an argument to be made that American buyers never really rejected the idea of the Cybertruck to begin with. Elon's politics aside, looks aside, valuation aside. I remember there being a ton of enthusiasm surrounding the Cybertruck reveal back in 2019 - which had a lot to do with its styling. People were intrigued by the notion of owning a pickup that looked more like a Hollywood movie prop than anything else.
We tend to look at depreciation as an indication of how poorly a vehicle has been received by the public, but that's not at all how it works. Besides, there are several examples of depreciation making a car genuinely competitive for the first time. And there are plenty of luxury and performance vehicles I would happily recommend purchasing second-hand, but would have a difficult time recommending at MSRP. This is well documented.
Photo: Tesla I suspect something similar is happening with the Cybertruck , even though the study doesn't tell us how much money actually exchanged hands. I've also never been entirely convinced that Tesla fully understood who their customers were in terms of buying Cybertrucks.
If you've been driving an F-150 all your life, towing your boat in the summertime, going on long road trips and so on, what would even be the point in switching to what would have been a much more expensive Tesla? And how much of what makes the Cybertruck interesting from an engineering and design standpoint would have been of any real consequence to you as a customer?
Let's switch it up and picture someone who's been driving a high-performance luxury SUV for the past 10 years and has never towed anything in their life. Now that's the type of person you're likely to get behind the wheel of a Cybertruck if you're Tesla . You think any Mercedes-AMG G 63 owners purchased their vehicles because of their off-road prowess? I doubt you'd even need both hands to count them.
There's a whole demographic of luxury car buyers for whom a vehicle's ability to generate an emotional response is more important than what that vehicle was engineered to do. The Cybertruck was always going to be right up their alley. Unfortunately for Tesla, there's no shortage of interesting cars available to people with $100,000 burning a hole in their pocket. The Cybertruck's novelty factor alone simply wasn't strong enough.
But things are very different on the used car market, where right now you could find yourself choosing between a Cybertruck and a relatively unremarkable midsize premium SUV, which can tilt the scales in favor of the former. Even I would be more inclined to put up with the Tesla's shortcomings under those circumstances.
Photo: Tesla Then there's the exclusivity factor. Had the Cybertruck sold in the hundreds of thousands, how much of what makes it a desirable proposition would have been lost in the process? We'll never know. As things stand right now, Tesla will depart the full-size pickup truck segment without ever having posed a serious threat to Detroit's Big 3. The Cybertruck is leaving with a whimper, not a bang.
In the end, it looks as though America's used car dealers are doing a way better job of selling the Cybertruck than Tesla ever has .
And come next year, if you'll want a brand-new, fully electric pickup truck, you can always call up Rivian and land yourself an R1T , unless you'd rather go for the Silverado EV/Sierra EV, or the Hummer EV Pickup.

By Alison Koo

Hyundai Motor’s logistics arm, Hyundai Glovis, has unveiled plans to broaden its third-party customer base as it goes all out to expand into air freight.
At the opening of its dedicated logistics centre in Incheon International Airport on Tuesday, Glovis said it saw opportunities from rising ecommerce volumes and demand for high value-added cargo transport.
Primarily an operator of car-carrier vessels, Glovis is expanding its third-party customer base through its air freight business. It transports APR’s cosmetics and SM Entertainment’s albums to North America and Europe, and provides air express services to Japan for major South Korean beauty brands.
A spokesperson said: “Our vision is to expand services that integrate land, sea, and air transportation, tailored to the specific characteristics and transportation objectives of customers’ cargo.”
Global air cargo demand rose 3.4% year on year in 2025 to a record high, according to IATA. The AI boom this year is expected to add to the growth, with more demand to transport servers and microchips.
Construction of a five-storey, 44,420 sq metre logistics facility – around 3km from the Incheon Airport Cargo Terminal – began in 2023, and by 2 November, Glovis had announced it had received Customs approval to handle express imports.

By: Staff Writer November 27, 2026
Zinc and lead producer Nyrstar is to halt production at its Budel zinc smelter in the Netherlands on Nov. 30 as rising energy costs make the operation unprofitable.
The smelter in the southeastern Netherlands has an annual zinc production capacity of 315,000 tonnes and employs about 500 people. Nyrstar, whose operating business is owned by commodities trader Trafigura, said Thursday it’s suspending production to stem losses.
“Market conditions for smelters remain extremely challenging, requiring policymakers to act quickly and decisively to retain strategic processing capacity,” Nyrstar CEO Matt Hadfield said in a news release .
Chinese smelting overcapacity, competition for concentrates and historically low treatment and refining charges are compounding the pressure of high energy costs on Western smelters. Nyrstar began a strategic review of Budel in September after the Dutch government omitted grid-cost relief for energy-intensive industries from its 2027 budget.
The company previously suspended production at Budel in January 2024 because of high energy costs and deteriorating market conditions. It announced a restart in April that year.
Shanghai Metals Market estimates the latest halt could cut refined zinc output by 200,000 to 220,000 tonnes if Budel remains idle throughout 2027.
Nyrstar expects no layoffs among permanent employees as a direct result of the halt and will maintain the site while it weighs its options. The company said in September it expected to complete the review by year-end. It hasn’t given a restart date.
